name: Logical reasoning and theorem proving
gist: Papers on making models reason step-by-step through logic puzzles, prove theorems, solve math, and identify errors in their own reasoning.
explain: Neural networks are good at pattern matching but often fail at tasks that require step-by-step logical reasoning. If you ask a model to solve a math problem or prove a theorem or find a logical error in an argument, it needs to think through the steps methodically, not just pattern-match. This is different from recognizing an object in an image or translating a sentence. It requires the model to break a problem into smaller pieces, reason about each piece, and combine the results — and to recognize when a line of reasoning is wrong.

The challenge is that logical reasoning requires symbolic manipulation — keeping track of abstract rules and facts and applying them correctly. Neural networks work with numbers and patterns, not symbols. Teaching them to do logic requires giving them ways to represent logical statements, rules for applying those statements, and ways to verify that the reasoning is correct. You also need to handle incomplete knowledge — in the real world, you never have all the facts, so the model has to fill in gaps by reasoning about what might be true given what it does know, without jumping to conclusions.

Researchers combine symbolic reasoning with neural learning. Some train models to output step-by-step proofs, where each step is explained and can be checked. Some use neuro-symbolic architectures, where a neural network learns patterns while symbolic engines handle the logic. Some use transformers (a type of neural network that can handle sequences) in new ways, teaching them to reason through transformations of knowledge step by step. Some teach models to generate test cases or counterexamples to verify their reasoning. The goal is a system that thinks methodically, can explain its reasoning, and can recognize when it is stuck.

papers.title: Enhancing Neural Theorem Proving via High-Quality Proof Selection and Verifier Feedback
papers.contribution: Fine-tuning on PSR-selected data achieves 84.8% Pass@64; with dynamic feedback-based optimization reaches 90.6% Pass@64, establishing new state-of-the-art for neural theorem proving in Isabelle.

papers.title: Expanding Reasoning Potential in Foundation Model by Learning Diverse Chains of Thought Patterns
papers.contribution: Only 10B-token data enables MoE model to improve 9.58% on AIME 2024-2025 and raise RL performance upper bound by 7.81%.

papers.title: Pursuing Minimal Sufficiency in Spatial Reasoning
papers.contribution: Significantly improves accuracy and achieves state-of-the-art performance on challenging spatial reasoning benchmarks with interpretable reasoning paths.

papers.title: Rethinking Code Similarity for Automated Algorithm Design with LLMs
papers.contribution: Demonstrates utility in improving LLM-based algorithm design via diversity-maintaining search and provides algorithm analysis tool.

papers.title: SLM-MUX: Orchestrating Small Language Models for Reasoning
papers.contribution: SLM-MUX achieves up to 13.4% improvement on MATH, 8.8% on GPQA, and 7.0% on GSM8K, with two SLMs outperforming Qwen 2.5 72B on some benchmarks.

papers.title: A Biologically Plausible Dense Associative Memory with Exponential Capacity
papers.contribution: Achieve exponential capacity in hidden units (provided visible units sufficiently larger) with distributed representations preserving class-discriminative structure.

papers.title: From Five Dimensions to Many: Large Language Models as Precise and Interpretable Psychological Profilers
papers.contribution: LLMs show remarkable accuracy capturing human psychological structure (R^2 > 0.88), using systematic two-stage reasoning that identifies key personality factors though fails to differentiate item importance within factors.

papers.title: MALICE: Memory-aware Loop Invariants Generation on Symbolic Execution Traces
papers.contribution: Evaluated on LIG-MM+, a benchmark featuring common operations on typical memory structures, \textsc{Malice} substantially outperforms existing approaches

papers.title: On the Reasoning Abilities of Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.contribution: Shows MDMs can solve all problems CoT-augmented transformers can, with inherent efficiency advantages for certain classes like regular languages.

papers.title: PERSISTENCE SPHERES: BI-CONTINUOUS REPRESENTATIONS OF PERSISTENCE DIAGRAMS.
papers.contribution: Persistence spheres achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance on clustering, regression, and classification across functional data, time series, graphs, meshes, and point clouds.

papers.title: Reading Between the Tokens: Improving Preference Predictions through Mechanistic Forecasting
papers.contribution: Probing internal knowledge via mechanistic forecasting improves prediction accuracy on election forecasting across 6 national elections.

papers.title: Stable and Scalable Deep Predictive Coding Networks with Meta Prediction Errors
papers.contribution: Achieves statistically significant improvements over conventional PCN and backpropagation across most architectures on CIFAR-10/100 and TinyImageNet while maintaining biological plausibility.
